name: Günter Blobel
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Blobel graduated medical school at 24 in 1960 and sailed to the US in 1962 to begin graduate studies. His PhD came in 1967 at age 31 and his signal hypothesis was proposed in 1975.
early_history_summary: Born to a wealthy veterinarian family in Silesia, Blobel fled the advancing Red Army in 1945 and settled in East Germany. He studied medicine at universities in Frankfurt, Kiel, Munich, and Tübingen, graduating in 1960. His elder brother Hans, a professor at the University of Wisconsin, helped him secure a fellowship to study in the US in 1962.
family_context_summary: Born into a wealthy family in Waltersdorf, Silesia; father was a veterinarian. One of eight children. The family fled the Red Army in 1945 and settled in Freiberg, East Germany.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a veterinarian; elder brother Hans became a professor of microbiology at the University of Wisconsin and helped Blobel secure a US fellowship.
evidence_summary: Blobel's Nobel Prize came in 1999 at age 63, decades after the age-26 cutoff. By 26, he was a recent medical school graduate beginning graduate studies in the US. His family was relatively affluent (father a veterinarian) and his brother's academic connections facilitated his move to America, but no material milestone had been achieved by age 26.

name: Pierre Bergé
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Bergé moved to Paris as a young man and was involved in leftist organizations and edited a short-lived magazine. He met Yves Saint Laurent in 1958 at age 28 and co-founded YSL in 1961 at age 31.
early_history_summary: Born on Oléron Island to a progressive teacher mother and a tax-office father, Bergé attended lycée in La Rochelle before moving to Paris. In his early Paris years he met Albert Camus and Sartre through leftist organizations, edited a short-lived magazine, and befriended artist Bernard Buffet.
family_context_summary: Mother was a progressive teacher who used the Montessori method; father worked for the tax office. Middle-class upbringing on Oléron Island.
evidence_summary: Bergé's fame came from co-founding Yves Saint Laurent in 1961 at age 31, well after the age-26 cutoff. By 26, he was a young Parisian involved in leftist politics and editing a short-lived magazine, with no independently verifiable material milestone.

name: Aruna Shanbaug
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Shanbaug was a junior nurse at KEM Hospital in Mumbai. She was sexually assaulted in November 1973 at age 25, leaving her in a vegetative state for 42 years. Her fame derives from being a victim, not from an achievement by age 26.
early_history_summary: Born to a Konkani Brahmin family in Haldipur, Karnataka, Shanbaug lost her father at age 10. She moved to Mumbai in 1966 at age 17 to pursue nursing, joined KEM Hospital as a staff nurse after training, and lived at the nursing hostel. She was engaged to a doctor at the hospital when she was assaulted in 1973.
family_context_summary: Born to a Konkani-speaking Brahmin family in Haldipur, Karnataka; father died when she was 10. She was the only sibling to complete higher education. The family faced financial hardship.
evidence_summary: Shanbaug is known for the tragic 1973 assault that left her in a vegetative state and the subsequent landmark euthanasia case. By age 26, she was a junior nurse with no notable achievement milestone. Her notability derives from victimhood and the legal case, not from personal accomplishment.

name: Subcomandante Marcos
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Marcos (allegedly Rafael Guillén) earned degrees from UNAM and possibly studied at the Sorbonne by his mid-20s. He entered the Lacandon jungle in late 1983 at age 26 to begin guerrilla organizing, but the Zapatista uprising did not occur until 1994 at age 37.
early_history_summary: Born in Tampico, Mexico, to an upper-middle-class furniture-store owner family, Marcos attended a Jesuit school and earned two degrees from UNAM. He may have studied philosophy at the Sorbonne. He became involved in Maoist revolutionary groups during his university years before entering the Lacandon jungle in late 1983.
family_context_summary: Identified by the Mexican government as Rafael Sebastián Guillén Vicente, born to the owner of a furniture chain in Tampico. Upper-middle-class upbringing with seven siblings. Jesuit-educated.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father owned the city's best-known furniture outlet; family was well-to-do in Tampico.
evidence_summary: Marcos's international fame came with the 1994 Zapatista uprising at age 37, well beyond the age-26 cutoff. By 26, he had academic credentials and was beginning clandestine guerrilla organizing, but no independently verifiable material milestone had been achieved.

name: Gherman Titov
milestone_by_age_26: At age 25, became the second human to orbit the Earth aboard Vostok 2 on August 6, 1961, completing 17 orbits over 25 hours and remaining the youngest person to fly in Earth orbit.
early_history_summary: Born in a rural Siberian village in Altai Krai, Titov was inspired by a pilot uncle to enter military aviation school in 1953 at age 18. He graduated as a jet fighter pilot in 1957 and was selected for the Soviet Union's first cosmonaut group in 1960, serving as backup to Yuri Gagarin before his own historic flight on Vostok 2.
family_context_summary: Born in the village of Verkhneye Zhilino in Altai Krai, Siberia. His father was a schoolmaster. His grandfathers helped build the first peasants' commune in Altai. The family lived in rural Siberia with modest means.
parent_family_domain_summary: An uncle who was a pilot inspired Titov to pursue aviation. No direct family aviation background documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet military aviation pipeline, cosmonaut selection, Space Race, jet pilot training
evidence_summary: Titov was born to a rural Siberian schoolteacher's family and entered military aviation school at 18, graduating as a jet fighter pilot in 1957. Selected for the first cosmonaut group in 1960, he served as Gagarin's backup before flying Vostok 2 at age 25, becoming the second human to orbit Earth. The Soviet space program's elite performance pipeline and the Space Race structural wave were the dominant advantages; family resources were modest but the state provided training.
starting_point: Born in a rural Siberian village in Altai Krai to a schoolmaster father; grandfathers were peasant commune founders in the Altai region.
current_position: Died on September 20, 2000 at age 65 in Moscow; final role was Colonel-General in the Russian Air Force and member of the State Duma.

trajectory.event: Entered the 9th Military Air School at Kustanai, Kazakhstan to begin aviation training.
Graduated as a jet fighter pilot from the Stalingrad Flying Academy and served in the Soviet Air Force.
Selected for the Soviet Union's first cosmonaut training group (TsPK-1) in March 1960.
Flew Vostok 2 on August 6, 1961, becoming the second human to orbit the Earth and the youngest person to fly in space, completing 17 orbits over 25 hours.
Graduated from the Zhukovsky Air Force Engineering Academy; cosmonaut career effectively ended after Gagarin's death led the Soviet government to ground Titov.
Retired from military service with the rank of Colonel-General.
Elected to the Russian State Duma as a member of the Communist Party of the Russian Federation.
Died of cardiac arrest in Moscow on September 20, 2000.

name: Abu Ali al-Anbari
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; al-Anbari completed military service and obtained a degree in Islamic studies at the University of Baghdad in 1982. By his mid-20s he was teaching sharia and serving as a mosque imam. His jihadi leadership role began in the early 2000s.
early_history_summary: Born in the Nineveh countryside of Iraq, al-Anbari (Abd al-Rahman Mustafa al-Qaduli) studied sharia at an institute in Tel Afar and fought in the Iran-Iraq War as a private. He obtained a degree in Islamic studies from the University of Baghdad in 1982, then worked as a religious education teacher and mosque imam in the mid-1990s.
family_context_summary: Born in the Nineveh countryside of Iraq; reportedly descended from the Quraysh tribe. Details of family economic status are not documented.
evidence_summary: Al-Anbari's notoriety came from his role as a senior ISIS commander in the 2010s, decades after the age-26 cutoff. By 26, he was a religious teacher and imam with no independently verifiable material milestone. His jihadi activities began in the early 2000s.

name: Fernando Santos
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Santos was a modest professional footballer playing as a left-back for Estoril and Marítimo in the Portuguese Primeira Liga. His managerial success came decades later, winning Euro 2016 with Portugal at age 62.
early_history_summary: Born in Lisbon, Santos joined Benfica's youth system at 16 and began his senior career with Estoril in 1973 at age 19. He played as a left-back for Estoril and Marítimo over eight seasons, accumulating 161 Primeira Liga appearances. He retired as a player around 1987 and began coaching at Estoril in 1988.
family_context_summary: Born in Lisbon, Portugal. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Santos was a journeyman left-back in the Portuguese league with no notable individual achievement by age 26. His fame derives from his later managerial career, particularly winning Euro 2016 with Portugal at age 62, long after the age-26 cutoff.

name: Richard R. Ernst
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Ernst was in graduate studies at ETH Zurich from 1957 to 1962. He received his PhD in 1962 at age 29 and won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1991 at age 58.
early_history_summary: Born in Winterthur, Switzerland, to an architect father, Ernst became fascinated with chemistry at age 13 after finding a case of chemicals in the attic. He studied chemistry at ETH Zurich from 1952 to 1956, completed military service, and began graduate studies in NMR spectroscopy under Hans Günthard and Hans Primas in 1957.
family_context_summary: Born in Winterthur, Switzerland; father was an architect teaching at the technical high school. Grandfather was a merchant who built the family home. Middle-class upbringing in a town with both artistic and industrial activities.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an architect and professor; an uncle who died in 1923 was a metallurgical engineer interested in chemistry whose chemicals sparked Ernst's interest in the field.
evidence_summary: Ernst's Nobel Prize came in 1991 at age 58, long after the age-26 cutoff. By 26, he was a graduate student at ETH Zurich working on NMR spectroscopy, with no independently verifiable material milestone. His family was middle-class and intellectually supportive, but no major achievement had occurred by age 26.

name: Trevor Jones
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Jones was working as a classical music reviewer for BBC Radio and Television and had begun graduate studies at the University of York. His first major film score was for the Oscar-winning short 'The Dollar Bottom' in 1981 at age 32.
early_history_summary: Born in Cape Town to a Cape Coloured family in District Six, Jones decided to become a film composer at age six. He attended the South African College of Music on a bursary from age 10, then won a scholarship to the Royal Academy of Music in London at 17 in 1967. After four years at the RAM, he worked as a classical music reviewer for the BBC before pursuing graduate studies at York University and the National Film and Television School.
family_context_summary: Born to a Cape Coloured family in Cape Town; family relocated to District Six under the Group Areas Act. Family suffered chronic poverty and substance abuse; mother was the sole breadwinner. Parents divorced when he was five.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; family had no notable musical or film industry background.
evidence_summary: Jones's career as a film composer took off in the 1980s with scores for Excalibur (1981) and The Dark Crystal (1982), well after the age-26 cutoff. By 26, he was a BBC music reviewer and graduate student. His early life was marked by apartheid-era poverty in District Six, but he showed exceptional determination, winning a scholarship to the Royal Academy of Music at 17.

name: Dietrich Mateschitz
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Mateschitz was still a university student at age 26, having spent ten years earning a marketing degree from the Vienna University of Economics and Business, which he completed in 1972 at age 28. He founded Red Bull in 1984 at age 40.
early_history_summary: Born in Styria, Austria, to two schoolteachers who separated when he was young, Mateschitz lived independently from his teenage years. He spent a decade at university, working as a ski instructor and in manual labor, before graduating with a marketing degree in 1972. He then worked in marketing at Unilever and Blendax before discovering Krating Daeng in Thailand in 1982.
family_context_summary: Born to two elementary school teachers in Styria, Austria; parents separated when he was young. From his teenage years, he lived independently away from his family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; parents were schoolteachers with no business or beverage industry background.
evidence_summary: Mateschitz founded Red Bull at age 40 in 1984, becoming a billionaire decades after the age-26 cutoff. By 26, he was still a university student with no material achievement. His parents were schoolteachers who separated when he was young, and he supported himself through ski instructing and manual labor during his prolonged studies.

name: Abdul Ahad Mohmand
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Mohmand was serving as a fighter pilot in the Afghan Air Force by age 26. He was selected for the Interkosmos program in 1988 and flew to space in August 1988 at age 29, becoming the first Afghan astronaut.
early_history_summary: Born in Sardeh Band, Ghazni Province, Afghanistan, Mohmand completed Habibia High School and entered Kabul Polytechnic University in 1976 at age 17. After graduating in 1978, he was drafted into the military and sent to the Soviet Union for pilot training at Krasnodar and Kyiv military aviation schools. He returned to Afghanistan in 1981 and rose through the Afghan Air Force ranks.
family_context_summary: Born in a remote village in Ghazni Province, Afghanistan. Belongs to the Momand tribe of the Pashtun ethnic group. Family economic background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Mohmand's historic spaceflight occurred in 1988 at age 29, after the age-26 cutoff. By 26, he was a military pilot in the Afghan Air Force with no independently verifiable material milestone. His selection for the Interkosmos program came in 1988, selected from over 400 candidates.

name: Bobby Orr
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26, Orr had won two Stanley Cups (1970, 1972), three Hart Trophies as NHL MVP, six consecutive Norris Trophies as best defenceman, two Conn Smythe Trophies as playoff MVP, and two Art Ross Trophies as league scoring champion, revolutionizing the defenceman position.
early_history_summary: Born in Parry Sound, Ontario, to a working-class family, Orr started organized hockey at age five and was noticed by NHL scouts at age twelve. At fourteen he joined the Oshawa Generals, the Bruins' junior affiliate, and debuted with the Boston Bruins in 1966 at age 18. He won the Calder Trophy as rookie of the year and began an unprecedented run of dominance, winning his first Norris Trophy at age 20 and his first Stanley Cup and Hart Trophy at age 22.
family_context_summary: Born in Parry Sound, Ontario. Father Doug Orr was a former hockey prospect who served in the Royal Canadian Navy in WWII and worked at a CIL dynamite factory. Mother was Arva Steele. Working-class family with five children. Grandfather Robert Orr was a pro soccer player from Northern Ireland.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Doug Orr had been a hockey prospect invited to join the Atlantic City Seagulls in 1942 but turned it down for naval service. Grandfather was a top-tier soccer pro. Family had deep sports culture but no financial advantage.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Oshawa Generals junior pipeline, Boston Bruins scouting, Bucko McDonald coaching, Wren Blair mentorship, NHL prodigy, Canadian hockey ecosystem
evidence_summary: Orr was a hockey prodigy from a working-class Parry Sound family; his father had been a hockey prospect and his grandfather a pro soccer player. NHL scouts noticed him at age twelve, and the Boston Bruins invested heavily in his development, arranging for him to play junior hockey at Oshawa from age 14. Coach Bucko McDonald moved him to defence and taught him the position, while Bruins scout Wren Blair managed his career trajectory. By age 22, Orr had won the Stanley Cup, Hart Trophy, Norris Trophy, Art Ross Trophy, and Conn Smythe Trophy in a single season, an unprecedented feat. The Bruins' elite performance pipeline and Orr's extraordinary skating and scoring ability were the dominant advantages.
starting_point: Born in Parry Sound, Ontario to a working-class family; father was a WWII Navy veteran and dynamite factory worker who had been a hockey prospect, mother was Arva Steele.
current_position: Retired from professional hockey since 1978; former president of Orr Hockey Group player agency (acquired by Wasserman Media Group in 2018); active in charitable works and junior hockey coaching; widely regarded as one of the greatest hockey players of all time.

trajectory.event: Signed with the Boston Bruins organization and joined the Oshawa Generals junior hockey team, competing against players four to six years older.
Debuted with the Boston Bruins in the NHL, winning the Calder Memorial Trophy as rookie of the year and making the NHL Second All-Star team.
Won the first of a record eight consecutive Norris Trophies as the NHL's best defenceman, despite playing only 46 games due to injury.
Won the Stanley Cup with the Bruins, scoring the iconic overtime clinching goal; became the only player to win four major NHL awards in one season (Hart, Norris, Art Ross, Conn Smythe).
Recorded 139 points (37 goals, 102 assists) setting still-standing records for points and assists by a defenceman in a single season; won second consecutive Hart Trophy.
Won second Stanley Cup with the Bruins and second Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP, becoming the award's first two-time winner.
Named MVP of the inaugural Canada Cup international tournament despite severely damaged knees; signed with Chicago Black Hawks as a free agent.
Inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame at age 31, the youngest inductee at that time.
